android.desc: Sync your Ricoh GR images to your phone in seconds. Connect over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, browse photo thumbnails, and tap to download. Not for you? Request a refund from Google Play within 48 hours, no questions asked. Within 7 days, email me the order number from your Google receipt and I'll refund it. FEATURES - Remembers your camera. Tap to connect. Multiple cameras supported. - Turns on the camera for you. Pair a GR III, IIIx or GR IV over Bluetooth and Eureka can power it on and turn on Wi-Fi without you ever reaching for the camera. - Fast browsing. Thumbnails for JPEG and RAW (DNG) files load straight from the camera, so you can find the shot without downloading everything. - Full-resolution viewer. Pinch, zoom and swipe at full quality before deciding what to keep. - One tap, or the whole shoot. Download a single photo or a batch. Transfers run in the background so you don't have to wait with the app open. - Remembers what you downloaded. Download all photos or just what's new after a shoot. - RAW support. DNG files land ready for Lightroom, Snapseed or whatever you edit in. HOW IT WORKS 1. Open Eureka and add your camera: Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. 2. Tap your camera to connect. 3. Browse your photos and tap to download. Downloads go to the Eureka folder under Pictures. To back them up to Google Photos, open that folder in Photos and turn on backup. SUPPORTED CAMERAS Ricoh GR II, GR III, GR IIIx and GR IV (GR2, GR3, GR3x, GR4), including the HDF editions and the GR IV Monochrome. PERMISSIONS AND PRIVACY Android requires the location permission to scan for Wi-Fi networks, so Eureka asks for it when you add a camera over Wi-Fi. The app never uses GPS and has no analytics. If you experience a crash or issue with the app, please use "Send feedback" in Settings to send a diagnostic log. ABOUT Eureka is built and maintained by one GR shooter. Found a bug or want a feature? Email me. The app is actively developed and I would love to hear from you. Eureka is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Ricoh Imaging. RICOH and GR are trademarks of Ricoh Company, Ltd.

I've had issues with my camera manufacturer's app for syncing photos on Android for years, so I finally built a super lightweight replacement which is faster and more reliable.[0] I used it for a year or so before finally going through the hassle of publishing it to the Play Store.

The app has a very limited audience. In the first month, I've had approximately 28 purchases. If I had to find 20 people to use the app for a couple weeks before I could publish, it wouldn't have been published.

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=me.johnmaguire.eureka
quotes.story_title: Android App Devs now require 20 people to test before publishing to Play Store
